exposure: Combined warming strategies (warmed IV fluids and forced-air warming - AW)
cohort: The study included 78 pregnant women undergoing cesarean delivery with spinal anesthesia.
finding: Combined modalities of active warming (warmed IV fluids and forced-air warming) were most effective in preventing perioperative hypothermia in mothers undergoing cesarean section.
mod_finding: The study focused on women undergoing cesarean delivery, and compared warming strategies during this mode of birth, finding no significant differences in neonatal outcomes based on the maternal warming strategy.
cross-section timing: Intraoperatively and for 30 minutes after surgery
birth_weight: Measured, but specific criteria for inclusion based on weight are not mentioned.
